title: Completed constant coefficients and finite reduction
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme, $A$ a commutative Noetherian ring, and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal. For an $A$-module $M$ write $\underline M$ for the sheafification of the constant presheaf with value $M$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on $T_{\Proet}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $B=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\underline{A/I^n}$, with its canonical $\underline A$-algebra structure. Then $B$ is flat over $\underline A$ (tensoring with $B$ preserves short exact sequences), and for every $a\geq1$ the canonical reduction map gives an isomorphism
$$
B\otimes_{\underline A}^L\underline{A/I^a}\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline{A/I^a}.
$$
If $A/I^a$ has a bounded finite-projective $A$-module resolution $F^\bullet$, then $B\otimes_{\underline A}\underline{F^\bullet}$ represents this reduction, with every term a direct summand of a finite sum of $B$. When every $A/I^n$ is finite, the locally constant sheaf $\underline{A/I^n}$ is the sheaf $(P_n)_T$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], so $B=A_T$ and the reduction identifies $A_T\otimes_{\underline A}^L\underline{P_a}$ with $(P_a)_T$.

source.place: Tag 093M (lemma-completion-flat), applied also to I^a with its cofinal power filtration; Tag 093J (lemma-constant-exact) for the resolution.

proof.text: For each object $U$ of the small site, put $M_n(U)=\underline{A/I^n}(U)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-section-properties] (3) with the Noetherian quotient ring $R=A/I^n$ and its free rank-one module $M=R$: $M_n(U)$ is flat over $A/I^n$. Apply (1) with $R=A$ to the surjection $A/I^{n+1}\to A/I^n$ and its kernel: all sectionwise transition maps are surjective. Scalar multiplication by $I^n$ vanishes because it already vanishes on the constant presheaf. The quotient is Noetherian: an ideal of $A/I^n$ is the image of its inverse-image ideal in $A$, so images of finite generators generate it. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-limit-flat-modules] applies, and gives $B(U)=\lim_n M_n(U)$ flat over $A$, and the natural isomorphism $Q\otimes_A B(U)\cong\lim_n Q\otimes_A M_n(U)$ for every finite $A$-module $Q$. The equality for $B(U)$ follows from its limit definition: a compatible family of sections glues component by component. All these maps commute with restriction in $U$.

source.place: Tag 093M, lemma-completion-flat, first paragraph; Tags 093J and 093L; More on Algebra Tag 0912, lemma-limit-flat, including its tensor clause

proof.text: Regard $B$ as a presheaf of modules over the constant presheaf of rings $U\mapsto A$, rather than assuming that $B(U)$ is flat over $\underline A(U)$. Tensor products and finite limits of these presheaf modules are computed objectwise, so flatness of every $B(U)$ in step 1 makes tensoring this presheaf preserve finite limits. Apply [lem-pc-sites-modules-sheafification-flat] to this presheaf ring and module. Their sheafifications are $\underline A$ and $B$; the latter is already a sheaf, so its sheafification is itself by the universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Its induced $\underline A$-action is the canonical one, since both actions extend the constant $A$-action. Hence $B$ is flat over $\underline A$ in the sense of [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules].

source.place: Tag 03ES, lemma-flatness-presheaves (objectwise argument written here), and Tag 03ET, lemma-flatness-sheafification; the first paragraph of Tag 093M

proof.text: Fix $a\ge1$ and put $Q=A/I^a$. It is finite as an $A$-module (generated by $1$) and finitely presented: finitely many generators of $I^a$ give a presentation $A^r\to A\to Q\to0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-section-properties] (2), $Q\otimes_A M_n(U)=\underline{(A/I^a)\otimes_A(A/I^n)}(U)$. The maps $\bar x\otimes\bar y\mapsto\overline{xy}$ and $\bar z\mapsto\bar1\otimes\bar z$ identify this ordinary tensor with $A/(I^a+I^n)=A/I^{\min(a,n)}$: changing a representative by an element of $I^n$ changes the second factor by zero, and changing it by an element of $I^a$ gives $\bar1\otimes t=\bar t\otimes\bar1=0$. Balancing also gives $\bar x\otimes\bar y=\bar1\otimes\overline{xy}$, so the maps are well-defined and inverse. For $n\ge a$ the transition maps are the identity of $\underline Q(U)$. A compatible family is therefore uniquely determined by its level-$a$ value, with earlier values its quotient images. Step 1 gives the natural isomorphism $B(U)\otimes_A Q\to\underline Q(U)$, explicitly $b\otimes\bar x\mapsto\pi_a(b)\bar x$. It is the cokernel of $B(U)^r\xrightarrow{(f_1,\ldots,f_r)}B(U)$, where $f_j$ generate $I^a$. The sheaf tensor $B\otimes_{\underline A}\underline Q$ is the same cokernel after sheafification: the presentation $\underline A^r\to\underline A\to\underline Q\to0$ follows from (1) and (2), and tensoring is right exact by step 2. Cokernels are sheafified sectionwise cokernels by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Since the displayed sectionwise cokernel is already the sheaf $\underline Q$, this proves that the ordinary sheaf-tensor reduction is an isomorphism, with precisely the displayed projection-and-multiplication formula.

source.place: Tag 093M, canonical quotient identifications; alternative derivation from the tensor clause of More on Algebra Tag 0912 and Tag 093K, lemma-tensor-with-finitely-presented

proof.text: The complex $B[0]$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]: tensoring any acyclic complex with it is just degreewise tensoring by the exact functor of step 2. Exactness preserves the kernels and images defining its cohomology, so that cohomology remains zero in every degree. By [def-weil-derived-tensor], choose the identity K-flat resolution of the first factor $B[0]$. Its derived tensor with $\underline Q[0]$ is represented by the ordinary tensor of step 3. The canonical derived reduction is represented by $b\otimes\bar x\mapsto\pi_a(b)\bar x$, and hence is an isomorphism. No finite-projective resolution of $Q$ is needed for this assertion.

Now suppose $F^\bullet\to Q[0]$ is a bounded resolution by finite projective $A$-modules. For each term choose a finite generating set and the resulting surjection $A^{r_i}\to F^i$. Projectivity [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] lifts $1_{F^i}$ across this surjection, giving maps $F^i\to A^{r_i}\to F^i$ with composite identity. The constant-sheaf functor preserves their composite; by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-section-properties] (2), with $M=A$ and $Q=A^{r_i}$, their sections are $\underline A(U)\otimes_A A^{r_i}=\underline A(U)^{r_i}$, compatibly with restriction, so finite free constant sheaves are $\underline A^{r_i}$. Tensoring these two maps with $B$ gives $B\otimes_{\underline A}\underline{F^i}\to B^{r_i}\to B\otimes_{\underline A}\underline{F^i}$ with composite identity. Thus each term is the asserted finite retract. Apply (1) to the exact sequences of cycles and boundaries of the augmented resolution: $\underline{F^\bullet}\to\underline Q[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Tensoring by the exact functor of step 2 preserves those sequences, so $B\otimes_{\underline A}\underline{F^\bullet}\to B\otimes_{\underline A}\underline Q[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Its composite with step 3 represents the derived reduction of step 4. The complex is bounded because $F^\bullet$ is bounded.

source.place: Tag 093J, lemma-constant-exact; finite retract and tensor calculation from the splitting definition of projectivity

proof.text: For a finite discrete ring $P$, let $C_P$ be its constant presheaf and $L_P(U)=\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|U|),P)$, the presheaf of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. The natural map $C_P\to L_P$ sends an element to its constant function. A function in $L_P(U)$ has finitely many clopen fibres in $|U|$, by the quotient topology on $\pi_0$ and discreteness of $P$. These clopen open subschemes form a finite covering of $U$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]; on each fibre the function is constant. For any sheaf of rings $H$ and presheaf ring map $C_P\to H$, extend it to $L_P\to H$ by gluing on this fibre cover the image of the respective constant value. The fibres are disjoint, so overlaps are empty; the sheaf condition for the empty covering gives exactly one section of $H$ on the empty object, hence agreement on overlaps; refinement by the intersections of fibre partitions proves compatibility with restriction, addition and multiplication. Any extension must have these restrictions and is unique by the sheaf condition. Hence $C_P$ and $L_P$ have the same universal maps to sheaves, and their sheafifications are canonically isomorphic by [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. The construction commutes with any map of finite rings, since both the function map and the constant map apply that ring map to each value. Apply this with $P=P_n=A/I^n$ for every $n$. The isomorphisms respect quotient transitions, so they identify their inverse limits $B=A_T$ as defined in [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and identify $\underline{P_a}=(P_a)_T$. Under these identifications the reduction of step 4 is exactly $A_T\otimes_{\underline A}^L\underline{P_a}\to(P_a)_T$. This identifies coefficient constructions; it does not identify $B$ with $\underline A$ or their module categories.

split_report.summary: Six steps prove flatness, canonical ordinary and derived reductions, the bounded finite-projective representative, and the finite coefficient interpretation. Existing constant-section, inverse-limit-flatness and sheafification-flatness nodes suffice; no new nodes. The sectionwise flatness argument uses the constant presheaf A before sheafification, avoiding an unsupported inference of flatness over underline A(U). Finite coefficient comparison uses clopen fibres rather than falsely assuming connected components open.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the first proof sentence of lem-weil-pbc-finite-reduction-reconstruction: the bounded finite-projective representative of P_a is scalar-extended to A_T with the canonical finite reduction.

tool_uses.why: General ringed-site sheafification preserves flatness, used as a black box; no node in this unit states this passage.
